idea-plugin.name: Claude Terminal Tab Persistence
idea-plugin.description:
Claude Terminal Tab Persistence for Rider / IntelliJ

Auto-restores your Claude Code terminal sessions across IDE restarts. The plugin tracks alive Claude sessions in ~/.claude/rider-plugin/active-sessions/ and, on next project open, spawns one fresh terminal tab per saved session running claude --resume <sid>.

3.0 redesign — own the terminal

The plugin now creates every Claude tab itself and assigns its session id at launch, so tab ↔ session identity is a stored fact from birth — no reflection, ancestry walks, or title guessing. Openness is simply "the tab is present in the tool window"; only an × closes a tab, while window-close, quit, crash, and reboot all reopen every open tab.

  • The plugin owns Claude tab titles. Every tab hosting a Claude session shows ✳ <name>, and the glyph animates while the session is thinking (mirroring Claude's own busy/idle status). Titles are continuously enforced — a tab clobbered to "Local" self-heals within half a second.
  • Names that stick. Display name priority: your explicit name (Rider's "Rename Tab" or /tab) > Claude's auto-generated topic name > the cached topic. Renames are adopted and persisted across restarts, never fought.
  • One file per alive session. active-sessions/<sid>.json — race-safe, no per-project file conflicts.
  • Bounded eviction backlog. session-backlog.json keeps the last 50 evicted sessions so you can recover them with /tabs-history.

Slash Commands

  • /tab — set this session's tab name explicitly (persists across restarts)
  • /tabs-status — live sessions + recent eviction backlog for the current project
  • /tabs-backup — explicit sync: write per-sid files for every alive Claude process
  • /tabs-history — browse the eviction backlog and print a resume command
  • /tabs-restore — list current per-sid files and print resume commands
  • /tabs-clear — clear active-sessions/ for the current project

Requirements: Rider / IntelliJ 2026.1+, Claude Code CLI, Node.js (for the bundled helper scripts).

Coexists with the JetBrains AI Assistant chat tool window (AI Agents panel: Junie / Claude Agent / Codex) and Anthropic's official Claude Code [Beta] plugin. This plugin manages terminal-launched Claude CLI sessions only — chat tabs in the AI Agents panel are managed by JetBrains.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
3.0.0 — Redone once more: own the terminal, assign the session id

Every earlier build created tabs it didn't fully own, then guessed which Claude session lived in each one (reflection PID digs, process-ancestry walks, title handshakes, cwd/time correlation). On Rider's reworked out-of-process terminal those signals are unreliable, so identity drifted and the restore/close logic kept mis-firing. 3.0 deletes the guessing entirely and replaces it with a mapping the plugin simply holds.

  • The plugin owns every Claude tab and assigns its session id at launch. New sessions run claude --session-id <uuid> with a plugin-minted UUID; restore runs claude --resume <sid>. Either way the plugin holds widget ↔ Content ↔ sid from birth — identity is a stored fact, never re-derived. Tabs opened via the terminal's own "Claude Code" agent button are captured too: a launch-time --session-id is injected and read back, and tabs created together are bound in creation (FIFO) order so a burst is never lost.
  • Openness = a present tab. A tab is open while its Content is present in the terminal tool window. An × removes the Content and drops exactly that one tab — no close event needed. Window-close, quit, crash, and reboot never shrink the set: the crash-atomic open-tabs snapshot is frozen during teardown, so every open tab reopens, named and animated, in order. Months-old sessions on disk never had a present tab, so they never flood back.
  • Titles driven natively. Reworked (agent-button) tabs are titled through their own TerminalView title, the same handle classic tabs use — so /tab names, auto topics, and the thinking animation all show identically regardless of how the tab was created.
  • Secrets kept out of names. A shell can set the terminal title to its full argv (including secret env values); titles that look like a command line or carry long secret-like tokens are never captured as a session name.
  • Deleted: the entire reflection/ancestry/title-heuristic matcher and the falsified process-attachment model and its reaper — the plugin never force-kills a process. It only reads and creates.

2.0.0 — Per-session tracking, title ownership, thinking animation

Ground-up rework: one file per alive session (active-sessions/<sid>.json) with crash-atomic (fsync) writes, a bounded eviction backlog, the ✳ name title + busy/idle animation, and restore in saved tab order. Superseded in identity handling by the 3.0 own-the-terminal model above.

1.0.18

Window-state serialization, worktree-resume transcript lookup, cross-project arbitration, two-poll-grace eviction. Superseded by the 2.0 and 3.0 redesigns.
